content.title: The Boys Season 5, Episode 3 Ending: Is Ryan Still Alive After Homelander's Beating?
content.text: Published Apr 15, 2026, 12:30 PM EDT Kyle is a senior writer at ScreenRant and has been part of the team for over two years. Having led coverage on The Walking Dead projects alongside Rick & Morty, Kyle is well versed in numerous genres. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Warning: This article contains SPOILERS for The Boys season 5, episode 3, "Every One of You Sons of Bitches."After an explosive opening two episodes, The Boys season 5 continued its momentum with another high-stakes episode that saw plenty of action and brutality. With episode 2 showing the supe virus in action, Soldier Boy's survival came as a real shock, as the V-One inside his blood saved him, setting up episode 3's main action. Both Homelander and The Boys were looking to find out if V-One was still in existence despite it being reportedly destroyed many years ago, prompting the central characters to seek out Stan Edgar, while Homelander sent his minions in pursuit. Meanwhile, Butcher was conducting his own plan involving Ryan, after the duo had a tense reunion. Butcher revealed that he wanted Ryan to lure out Homelander before throwing the supe virus at him, even though it would kill them both. Reluctantly, Ryan eventually accepted, but after Butcher lied about it being his destiny and not being strong enough to fight Homelander one-on-one, the young supe went to confront his father about his sins. Even though Homelander does still care about his son, The Boys season 5's time skip has made him more unhinged than ever, causing him to fight back when Ryan attacked him. Despite gaining the upper hand and leaving his son defenseless, Homelander proceeded to punch Ryan over and over with little remorse, leaving his lifeless body there until Butcher eventually found him. Why Homelander Beats Up Ryan In The Boys Season 5, Episode 3's Ending The young hero wanted to know the truth about what Homelander did to his mother, and since he could sense his heart racing through his powers, Ryan knew his father was lying. As a result, he attempted to push and even laser the antagonist, forcing Homelander to take defensive action, which was genuinely an attempt to defuse the situation at first. However, once Ryan delivered a punch that made him bleed, Homelander threw his son to the ground several times and pinned him down, before beginning to beat him up. While he could've easily walked away before throwing any punches, Homelander seemed hellbent on punishing his son, hence why he kept on going, even when Ryan was clearly too injured to fight back. The Boys season 5's trailers sparked theories about who Homelander was punching, as that slight look of hesitation before delivering the final blow suggested it was someone close. With context though, the scene is even worse than many might have imagined, as it shows just how far gone the villain truly is. Previously, Homelander went out of his way to try and form a relationship with his son, as he wanted Ryan to follow in his footsteps. Now though, he feels like his own destiny is more important, which is why he didn't have too many conflicted thoughts about pummeling his own flesh and blood. Is Ryan Still Alive After Homelander's Brutal Beatdown (& What Next)? Having barely survived the run-in with Homelander, Ryan's journey will surely switch to getting revenge on his father. While he's clearly not an experienced enough fighter to take him down in a fist fight, Ryan does have the strength and abilities to potentially kill Homelander, and with The Boys' help, it's possible. His last conversation with Butcher suggested the two were once again on bad terms, but considering The Boys' leader is the one who found him and will likely tend to his wounds, they may find common ground once again. Butcher even mentioned that they're the same thing, giving Ryan a reason to work with him, despite not fully trusting his stepfather. There is also a chance he collides with Butcher down the line, considering the latter is obsessed with wiping out all supes. He was willing to allow both himself and Ryan to die if it meant taking down Homelander, or so he claimed, and with Butcher becoming more like Homelander in The Boys season 5, he may wind up going too far. Therefore, if Ryan does somehow manage to survive the war against Homelander, his fight may not be over, and stopping Butcher could become his end goal. Until then, his next steps will be to regain his strength and pursue Homelander, hopefully with some more guidance this time. Homelander Is More Terrifying Than Ever In The Boys Season 5 Based on the previous four seasons, it didn't seem like Homelander could get any more terrifying, but season 5's version is the scariest yet. Although he's still desperate for approval, he seems to have found it internally, as his vision of Madelyn Stillwell was evidence that Homelander doesn't need the respect of others these days. In episode 2, he was still searching for Soldier Boy's acceptance, while previous installments saw him bothered by Stan Edgar's lack of fear. Now, he sees himself as a god that deserves the world, and he's far less insecure, even bathing in breast milk in front of Soldier Boy without feeling any sense of shame. Additionally, he could get his hands on V-One if there is any left in the world, which would essentially make him immortal. Gen V season 2 suggested Marie could potentially defeat Homelander, but other than her, only Soldier Boy, Butcher, and Ryan seem even remotely capable of murdering The Boys' main villain. As a result, the supe virus remains the world's best chance of getting rid of him, but if he acquires V-One, the virus becomes borderline useless, hence why the main group is so desperate to prevent Homelander from getting his hands on this substance. His recent scene with Ryan was just the latest sign that Homelander is more unhinged than ever, making this the most menacing iteration of the character yet without question. He's no longer driven by the love or admiration of others, and other than a few exceptions, he isn't taking prisoners either. The Seven leader even mentioned using those currently in internment camps as human test subjects to try and recreate V-One, showing that his main goal at the moment is immortality, and he'll let nothing stand in his way. While The Boys were able to survive the ambush on Stan Edgar's bunker, Stan was kidnapped by the Deep and taken to Homelander, which is a massive win for the villain. Alongside being one of the only people with expert knowledge about V-One and Vought's history, Stan has been a long-term foe of Homelander. Having him in custody means Homelander can try to extract as much information out of him as possible, and while Stan is one of the few characters in the show who isn't intimidated by the villain, he could use Zoe as leverage. Threatening to hunt her down would inevitably make Stan budge and force him to give up any information he knows. The Boys season 5, episode 3's ending really left the main heroes in a bleak place, as they have nothing but a file to help aid their mission, while Homelander seems to hold all the cards. Likewise, with Stan being one of the project's craftiest characters, he may even help the villains so that he can regain control of Vought. With Starlight also going her own way and Butcher still with Ryan, it looks like an uphill battle for the protagonists heading into The Boys season 5's halfway point.
